data_objects.name: mass_spectra
data_objects.meaning: A tab-separated collection of tandem mass-spectrum records, each associating a variable-length peak list with a molecular structure and precursor-ion metadata.

variables.name: identifier
variables.meaning: Dataset-assigned identifier for the spectrum record.

variables.name: mzs
variables.meaning: Comma-separated numeric vector of observed spectral-peak mass-to-charge coordinates, aligned by position with the intensities vector.

variables.name: intensities
variables.meaning: Comma-separated numeric vector of relative peak intensities, aligned by position with the mzs vector.

variables.name: smiles
variables.meaning: SMILES string describing the molecular structure associated with the spectrum; inspected values can include stereochemical notation.

variables.name: inchikey
variables.meaning: Fourteen-character InChIKey-derived molecular connectivity identifier recorded for the associated compound.

variables.name: formula
variables.meaning: Elemental formula of the parent molecule associated with the spectrum.

variables.name: precursor_formula
variables.meaning: Elemental formula recorded for the precursor ion, reflecting the adduct composition in inspected examples.

variables.name: parent_mass
variables.meaning: Mass recorded for the unadducted parent molecule.

variables.name: precursor_mz
variables.meaning: Mass-to-charge ratio recorded for the precursor ion selected for the spectrum.

variables.name: adduct
variables.meaning: Bracket notation for the precursor adduct and charge state, such as protonated [M+H]+ or sodiated [M+Na]+ species.

structure.description: The release is a single row-oriented TSV. Each row represents one spectrum record: mzs and intensities are parallel comma-separated vectors, while the remaining fields identify the associated compound and describe its parent and precursor ion. Multiple rows can refer to the same compound while carrying different spectra.

uncertainties: The permitted public subtree contains no documentation beyond the TSV, so column semantics are inferred from names, chemical conventions, and inspected values rather than an explicit data dictionary.

m/z and dalton units are conventional in mass spectrometry but are not declared within the file itself; parent_mass appears consistent with an unadducted molecular mass, but the file does not state whether it is specifically monoisotopic or how it was calculated.

Inspected spectra had equal-length mzs and intensities vectors and intensity maxima of 1.0, suggesting per-spectrum normalization, but vector alignment and the normalization procedure were not exhaustively validated.
Inspected inchikey values were 14 characters long and therefore appear to be the molecular-connectivity block rather than full InChIKeys; the truncation convention is not documented in the file.

The table does not expose acquisition details such as instrument, collision energy, ionization method, or provenance, so distinctions among repeated spectra for the same compound cannot be fully interpreted from this public file.
Protonated and sodiated positive-ion adducts were observed in bounded samples, but the complete set of adduct categories was not exhaustively enumerated.
annotation_notes: massspecgym.tsv contains a header plus 231104 data rows and has 10 tab-separated columns.
Inspection was bounded to the header, a small number of head, tail, and widely spaced records, and adduct values from several bounded row blocks.

Representative records showed variable peak counts, positional agreement between the two peak vectors, non-contiguous numeric suffixes in record identifiers, and repeated compound metadata across distinct spectrum rows.
